newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse not to charge for MDAX futures.
newsitem.headline: German bourse not to charge for MDAX futures.

text.p: The German DTB futures exchange said on Thursday it would not be charging for transactions involving futures on the MDAX index of medium-capitalised German companies for the rest of the year.
"This will make these futures...still more easily accessible to market participants," the DTB said in a statement.
DTB business manager Joerg Franke said the bourse was "not yet completely satisfied" with current turnover volumes of the MDAX future.
Overall trade in MDAX stocks has risen substantially since the introduction of the MDAX in January. The index now makes up around 14 percent of total trade in German shares.
Franke said the bourse saw the index future and the MDAX index as "long-term investments in the mid-cap market".
The DTB said it was considering whether it should introduce a designated market-making system for the MDAX future to increase liquidity still further.
